blanks.sentence: Modern players are faster, but the game also demands _____.
Players make choices under the _____ and intensities.
Compared with that of similar players, Neymar's brain showed _____ when he moved his ankle.
This pattern showed his _____ in moving his feet.
Clubs are showing growing interest in _____.
If players cannot store much information, coaches may make them feel mentally _____.
This challenge is introduced in a _____, such as training.
Control of a player's emotional state can be _____.
Before penalties, corners and free kicks, players are taught to _____.

multipleChoice.question: Which new performance factor are some football clubs examining?
options: The physical speed needed throughout a match
The athletic demands created by modern competitions
The mental activity involved in rapid, pressured decisions
The passion that makes football attractive to supporters

multipleChoice.question: What did the 2014 study observe when Neymar moved his right ankle?
options: His brain showed less activity than the brains of comparable players.
His brain reacted more slowly than those of comparable players.
His foot moved more accurately than those of comparable players.
His emotional response was weaker than those of comparable players.

multipleChoice.question: According to the neuroscientist, what did Neymar's reduced cortical activity indicate?
options: He was protecting his brain from the pressure of competition.
He was relying mainly on his emotional control during movement.
He needed less physical energy than other professional players.
He had mastered the movement so well that little conscious effort was needed.

multipleChoice.question: How may coaches respond when players struggle to hold a large amount of information?
options: They remove complex decisions until the players enter a competition.
They deliberately overload the players during a safe training session.
They measure the players' brainwaves after every difficult exercise.
They replace cognitive practice with sessions focused on physical speed.

multipleChoice.question: What contrast is central to the training approach described?
options: Players face controlled mental overload in training so they may improve in real matches.
Players practise without pressure before facing identical tasks in cup competitions.
Players first develop physically and then begin separate neurological training.
Players store match information but avoid using it during practice sessions.

multipleChoice.question: What view is expressed about the emotional side of performance?
options: It matters only during set pieces such as penalties and corners.
It is fixed by personality and therefore difficult for coaching to change.
It strongly influences performance but can be brought under greater control.
It becomes useful only when players stop making conscious decisions.

multipleChoice.question: What is the likely effect of having too much emotion during play?
options: It helps a player act automatically with less mental effort.
It makes accurate and concentrated play more difficult.
It allows a player to manage larger amounts of information.
It increases the value of physical training over brain training.

multipleChoice.question: Why are penalties, corners and free kicks especially suitable for focused mental coaching?
options: They are the only occasions when emotions affect a player's performance.
They require players to store more information than any other match situation.
They allow brain activity to stop briefly before physical movement begins.
They provide brief pauses in which players can manage their mental state.

multipleChoice.question: What is the purpose of mentioning difficulty in delivering an accurate corner?
options: To illustrate how scattered attention can weaken execution at a decisive moment
To prove that corners are mentally harder than penalties and free kicks
To show that brainwave measurement directly improves kicking technique
To suggest that technical ability becomes irrelevant in high-pressure situations

multipleChoice.question: What overall implication can be drawn from the discussion of small margins?
options: Brain training can remove the uncertainty from close football matches.
Emotional control matters more than skill in determining every match result.
Only major neurological changes are likely to affect competitive performance.
Small gains in focus may have an important effect on the final outcome.
